title: Evening quant snaplog
content:
Evening quick log — lightweight, messy. Goal: capture hypotheses and micro-experiments before I forget. Not for sharing yet.

2026-03-28 18:15 — context
- Trying small-series quantization checks on the 13B Llama-variant that passed CI (model v2.1.4). Running INT8 and hybrid-4bit on local devbox (A10G replica).
- Primary question: does per-channel symmetric quant + KV-cache-friendly remat preserve decoding stability on long prefix workloads (~1024 tokens)?

Recent runs (short notes):
1) run id: petra-q-0328-01
   config: int8 symmetric per-channel, no activation clamping, dynamic range computed on calibration batch of 128 sequences (seq len 512).
   perf: decode throughput ~260 tps (toy harness).
   quality: BLEU-like proxy (synthetic QA) drop ~3.7% vs fp16 baseline. Intermittent hallucination spikes at token 430-470.
   observations: KV cache size marginally larger (unexpected). Suspect indexing alignment bug in quantized KV serialization. Related to runtime PR 987?

2) run id: petra-q-0328-02
   config: 4bit hybrid (group-wise, 64), activation clamp to 6.0, reorder matmul path to fallback on small-matmul kernel.
   perf: 480 tps, cost down ~35% vs fp16.
   quality: proxy drop ~1.2%. Hallucinations reduced but not eliminated. Latency p95 increased when sequence > 768 (spike due to fallback).
   notes: fallback kernel triggers when token_count%64 != 0 — investigate pad-to-multiple heuristics.

Prompts & test set (quick paste):
- Short QA prompt template used for synthetic proxy: 
  "You are an assistant. Given the context and question, extract the single-sentence answer. Context: <passage> Question: <q>"
- 1k synthetic examples derived from CommonCrawl snippets + handcrafted counterfactuals (see linked artifact Red-TR-2026-03-20 eval set).

Quick debugging checklist (what to try next):
- [ ] Re-run petra-q-0328-01 with explicit KV cache alignment flags (runtime: --kv-align=64) to check if mysterious growth disappears.
- [ ] Add calibration set with longer tails (seq len up to 1024) to capture dynamic range for later tokens.
- [ ] Try symmetric per-channel but with 8-bit activations stored for first two layers (hybrid micro) to see if hallucination reduces.
- [ ] Run regression check against model v2.0.9 to confirm whether v2.1.4 introduced sensitivity.

Notes about evaluation signals (thinking aloud):
- BLEU-like proxy useful but brittle — need an LM-based scoring/regression (e.g., pairwise majority votes from 3 decodes) for hallucination detection.
- Also need to add perplexity delta with sample temperature 0.2 to surface overconfident wrong outputs.

Small idea: "prefix-preserving quantization"
- Hypothesis: clamp/scale calibrations focused on early-layer activations (first N attention blocks) will preserve prefix fidelity for long-context tasks while allowing aggressive quant in later layers.
- Quick plan: freeze first 4 layers to int8 but keep activations in fp16 for first 2 blocks, then hybrid 4-bit for blocks 5+. Compare decode fidelity on prefix-heavy tasks.

Operational reminders:
- Drop logs into /mnt/ssd/petra/q-experiments/ with subdir by date and run id. Keep raw logits + token traces for at least 48h.
- Upload promising run artifacts to GH blobstore and post short note in #applied-ml with run id.

Questions to ask Arjun (for tomorrow sync):
- Did you observe KV cache size increasing in your prod-sim microbench when enabling per-channel symmetric quant? Which kernel path was used?
- Are there any known issues in PR 987 that touch KV memory layout?

Mental TODO (tiny, informal):
- rip out the old pad-to-64 helper in micro-kernel, but keep toggle flag for rollback.
- Add tiny unit that verifies deserialize(serialize(kv)) yields identical offsets (quick CI test).

Raw excerpt of one failing decode (keeps context for later):
[seed=42873] prompt: "Context: ... long passage (512 tokens) ... Question: When did the treaty expire?"
fp16 baseline: "The treaty expired in 1939."
int8 run: "The treaty expired in 1963, according to the archived minutes." (hallucinated addition)
Notes: model adds spurious date clause — check attention weights around token 420 (do we see vanishing attention?).

End-of-day personal notes:
- Feeling slightly tired; prioritize reproductions tomorrow before over-tuning. Keep experiments small and reproducible.
- Leave a one-line summary in #applied-ml when at least one run with improved fidelity is found.

-- Petra
